scope: Wise integration API naming, layering, configuration, documentation, tests, UI page-object ownership, rendering-based static-content validation, and Vue styling conventions.
guidance: These are explicit, user-confirmed current policies. Their source-grounded corrections are verified above; no measured reviewer improvement or speculative historic reviewer-failure claim is made.

evidence: Read preserved round-2 snapshot, reviewer prompt, investigation records, and finding-validation result; the proposal treats F29-F45 as current user policies, not evidence of historic reviewer failure or measured improvement.
F29-F32: IntegrationsGqlApi is provider-neutral; root documentation is neutral; it depends only on WiseIntegrationService; exposed account identifiers are documented opaque.
F33-F34: WiseApiClient and typed WiseProperties are in business.integrations.wise; properties use sa.integrations.wise and mocks use the same prefix.
F35: dedicated SetupWiseIntegrationMutationTest, VerifyWiseIntegrationTokenMutationTest, and WiseIntegrationQueryTest exist with authorization/business-flow nesting.
F36-F37: unsupported direct-route UI coverage is absent; UserNavigationMenuFullStackTest owns exact regular-user menu assertions and menu navigation; Wise page workflows open routes directly.

F38: WiseIntegrationFullStackTest has rendering reports for static views; IntegrationsPage.ProviderCards has only Setup/View interactions, with branding/description assertions and their caller removed.

F39-F43: setupAccounts is an action-named stub helper; direct client and logging tests, shared IntegrationCards wrapper, and duplicate GraphQlFailureMocks utility are absent; WireMock-backed WiseIntegrationServiceTest and PlaywrightExtensions.withFailedGqlApiResponse are present.
F44-F45: IntegrationPage has no frontend authorization gate while GraphQL operations retain RequiredAuth; integration styles are scoped Vue SFC styles and the external SCSS file is absent.

F40 remains faithful despite the original safety requirement: GraphQlOperationLoggingInstrumentation still uses only parameters.operation or anonymous and does not log raw queries; the user explicitly requested removal of its dedicated test.

dispositions.feedback: this is not "wise integraiton" any longer, but just "integrations"
dispositions.evidence: Current provider-neutral API namespace is `IntegrationsGqlApi` in `app/src/main/kotlin/io/orangebuffalo/simpleaccounting/business/api/integrations/IntegrationsGqlApi.kt:20`.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed current naming policy; no historic reviewer-failure theory is asserted.
dispositions.lesson: Name the extensible integration API after the provider-neutral integrations domain, not its first provider.

dispositions.feedback: No, "wise" is only relevant for "WiseIntegrationGqlDto", IntegrationsGqlDto is about all integrations user can configure
dispositions.evidence: `IntegrationsGqlApi.kt:25` documents configurable integration providers, while `IntegrationsGqlDto` at line 85 contains the provider-specific `wise` DTO.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed API-documentation boundary; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Made the root description provider-neutral and retained Wise-specific wording only for Wise DTOs.
dispositions.lesson: Document integration root DTOs as extensible provider collections; reserve provider names for provider-scoped types.

dispositions.feedback: api client should be internal to the wise integraiton service. all other parts of the system, in particular api here, should interact with the busienss service only
dispositions.evidence: `IntegrationsGqlApi.kt:23,35` injects only `WiseIntegrationService`; `WiseIntegrationService.kt:12` owns the internal `WiseApiClient`, declared `internal` in `WiseApiClient.kt:16`.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed layering policy; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Restricted GraphQL API interaction to `WiseIntegrationService`; made the client service-internal.
dispositions.lesson: Keep provider clients internal to their business integration service; APIs depend only on that service.

dispositions.feedback: do not say that about ids. they are opaque for this api clients and just pass through
dispositions.evidence: `IntegrationsGqlApi.kt:67` and line 74 describe selection and returned identifiers as opaque values.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed public API documentation policy; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Changed identifier documentation to state opacity and pass-through semantics.
dispositions.lesson: Describe third-party identifiers exposed by the API as opaque unless clients are meant to interpret them.

dispositions.feedback: client and properties should move to `business.integrations.wise` package, they are part of it
dispositions.evidence: `WiseApiClient.kt:1` and `WiseProperties.kt:1` are in `business.integrations.wise`; the former `infra/thirdparty/wise` source is absent from the current tree.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed ownership/package policy; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Moved the Wise client and properties into the Wise business-integration package.
dispositions.lesson: Place provider-specific client/configuration implementation with its owning business integration when it is not shared infrastructure.

dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed configuration namespace policy; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Updated the typed Wise configuration prefix and corresponding mock configuration usage.
dispositions.lesson: Root integration-provider configuration under `sa.integrations.<provider>` using typed configuration properties.

dispositions.feedback: we should have a class per every mutation. plus a class per resonable level of data queeries (integrations.wise in this case)
dispositions.evidence: Separate tests exist at `SetupWiseIntegrationMutationTest.kt:26`, `VerifyWiseIntegrationTokenMutationTest.kt:25`, and `WiseIntegrationQueryTest.kt:17`; each preserves authorization/business-flow nesting.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed test-organization policy; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Split mutation and provider-query coverage into dedicated test classes.
dispositions.lesson: Organize GraphQL tests by mutation and by reasonable query hierarchy level rather than one broad API test class.

dispositions.feedback: this test is bad. we have a dedicated menu test that verifies the exact list of the menu items. direct opening we do not care - api-level tests are verifying access to actual data/functions, and what will happen on ui is not our concern for unsupported cases. no maintenance efforts should be spent on this.
dispositions.evidence: `WiseIntegrationFullStackTest.kt` contains no administrator or unsupported-direct-route scenario; exact regular-user menu coverage is in `UserNavigationMenuFullStackTest.kt:41-58`, and API authorization tests cover unsupported actors, e.g. `SetupWiseIntegrationMutationTest.kt:43-70`.
dispositions.hypothesis: User-confirmed test-scope policy; no historic cause is asserted.
dispositions.action: Removed unsupported-route UI coverage while retaining dedicated menu and API authorization coverage.
dispositions.lesson: Do not maintain UI tests for unsupported direct routes when dedicated menu and API authorization coverage own those concerns.
